statement: For every n >= 3 and every normalized strictly increasing Gilbreath sequence S in G_n, if its full two-sided valid-extension set K_S is not the candidate parity interval C_S, then |K_S| >= 10. The bound is sharp, attained by S=(2,3,5,9,15). Consequently |K_S| <= 9 holds exactly when K_S=C_S and A(S)<=7; this reduces the still-unresolved original classification to the four small ordered anti-diagonal types stated in evidence/threshold_lemma.md, without claiming an explicit classification of all top rows realizing those types.
contribution: A sharp all-length gap theorem for defective valid-extension sets and a finite anti-diagonal reduction of the source's open width-at-most-nine classification. The proof isolates a realizability constraint (zero-tail rigidity) absent for arbitrary folding tuples. The cited source does not state this gap theorem, and a limited current search found no separate primary source claiming it; this is bounded novelty language, not proof of priority.
